menu.quit_confirm.old: This is the door. One More Turn is a different button, and it appears after you have already won.
menu.quit_confirm.new: Quit the game? One More Turn is a different button. It appears after you win.
menu.quit_confirm.why: Lead with the question; keep the joke short.

menu.preset.evening_standard.seats.old: Swans, one early-war bird, one schemer. Take one of those seats and the chair refills.
menu.preset.evening_standard.seats.new: Seats the Swans, one early-war empire and one schemer. Play one of them yourself and a random empire takes the empty chair.
menu.preset.evening_standard.seats.why: Old line did not say what happens.

menu.toggle.seat_swans.tip.old: Checked by default. Unchecking it is a setting.
menu.toggle.seat_swans.tip.new: Put The Pale Supremacy in the galaxy. On by default. Turning it off is an easier game, and you know it.

difficulty.nestling.tip.old: The AI is smaller, and polite about it. It will not come for you first. The card says -25% industry and research.
difficulty.nestling.tip.new: AI empires get -25% industry and research and never attack you first. For learning the birds.

difficulty.flighted.tip.old: No gifts to either side. If you lose, it is yours.
difficulty.flighted.tip.new: The standard game. No handicap for either side. If you lose, it is yours.

difficulty.honk_admiral.tip.old: The AI receives the printed bonuses and may read your ship designs. Be angry at a number. The number is listed.
difficulty.honk_admiral.tip.new: AI empires get +20% industry, +20% research, and can see your ship designs. Printed cheats: be angry at the number.
difficulty.honk_admiral.tip.why: 'Printed bonuses' were not printed. Verify numbers vs code.

difficulty.lights_off_ledger.tip.old: +40% industry, +40% research, +20% growth, your designs, your colonies, your fleets. Every modifier is printed. None of them are gentle.
difficulty.lights_off_ledger.tip.new: AI empires get +40% industry, +40% research, +20% growth, and can see your designs, colonies and fleets. Every modifier is printed. None of them are gentle.
difficulty.lights_off_ledger.tip.why: Make the sentence parse; same numbers.

star.neutron.name.why: Star class label; the pun hid the class.

climate.toxic.name.why: Planet row must read as hostile at a glance.

climate.radiated.name.why: Planet row must read as hostile at a glance.

special.old_nest.tip.old: The first colony here is handed a low tech you do not have.
special.old_nest.tip.new: The first empire to colonise this planet receives one low-tier tech it does not have.

special.pretty_rocks.tip.old: +5 credits a turn. Shiny, and annoyingly liquid.
special.pretty_rocks.tip.new: +5 credits a turn. Shiny, and it sells.

special.spare_nest.tip.old: The first colony starts at two pop.
special.spare_nest.tip.new: A colony founded here starts with 2 pop instead of 1.

building.grand_nest.tip.old: The capital. It counts for more than it should, and it knows.
building.grand_nest.tip.new: Your capital. +3 food, +5 industry, +3 research, +5 credits, +2 scan range, and ships can be built here.

building.boot_barracks.tip.old: A garrison, and a slow refill of marines.
building.boot_barracks.tip.new: Garrison of 4 marines against invasion, regrowing 2 per turn.

building.feed_hall.tip.old: Food, from a building, if the climate will not.
building.feed_hall.tip.new: +2 food, whatever the climate thinks of farming.

building.research_roost.tip.new: +1 research per scientist and +3 flat. Labs that lab.
building.research_roost.tip.why: Effect first, joke kept as tail.

building.horizon_perch.tip.old: Three launchers of whatever you currently believe in.
building.horizon_perch.tip.new: Planet defence: 3 launchers firing your best Horizon missile, unlimited ammo.
building.horizon_perch.tip.why: Old line hid that it is a defence.

building.colony_mantle.tip.old: A shield for the nest. Bombardment is halved.

building.richer_dirt.tip.old: Farmers, fed better by the dirt itself.

building.second_clutch.tip.old: Growth, up by half, on this colony.

building.tireless_picks.tip.old: Robots. They do not call in sick, and they do not start religions.
building.tireless_picks.tip.new: +1 industry per worker and +5 flat. Robots: they do not call in sick, and they do not start religions.

building.loud_abacus.tip.old: Scientists, plus a machine that interrupts them productively.
building.loud_abacus.tip.new: +1 research per scientist and +5 flat. A machine that interrupts the scientists, productively.

building.more_perch.tip.old: One more pop per size, on this world.
building.more_perch.tip.new: +1 max population per planet size at this colony.

building.talon_batteries.tip.old: Four heavy Talons, aimed by a planet.
building.talon_batteries.tip.new: Planet defence: 4 Primary-mounted beams of your best Talon.

building.gravity_manners.tip.old: The gravity penalty on this world packs up and leaves.
building.gravity_manners.tip.new: Removes this world's gravity penalty to job output.

building.night_lab.tip.old: Ten research, whether or not anyone is on shift.
building.night_lab.tip.new: +10 research, whether or not anyone is on shift.

building.climate_lever.tip.new: +1 food per farmer. Weather, by policy.

building.ugly_perch.tip.old: A gun platform with a shield. Ships built here cost less.
building.ugly_perch.tip.new: Orbital fortress: 400 hull, 6 of your best Talons, your best ship shield. Ships built here cost 10% less.

building.flock_brain.tip.old: Scientists here, up by two each.
building.flock_brain.tip.new: +2 research per scientist at this colony.

building.storm_mantle.tip.new: Planet shield 10. Bombardment damage cut to a quarter.

building.second_shift_hall.tip.old: The night crew does not care about your narrative arc.
building.second_shift_hall.tip.new: +1 industry per worker and +3 flat. The night crew does not care about your narrative arc.

building.roost_gate.tip.old: One turn between any two gates you own. The map does not grow a road.
building.roost_gate.tip.new: Fleets travel between any two of your Roost Gates in one turn.

building.departure_roost.tip.old: The door out. Starting it is announced. Finishing it is the victory.
building.departure_roost.tip.new: The Exodus victory project. Everyone is told when you start it. Finishing it wins the game.

notify.starvation.old: The granary is a rumour. {place} is losing people.

notify.strike.old: The treasury hit the floor. Industry sulks next turn.
notify.strike.new: Treasury empty. Strike: industry -25% next turn.

notify.nest_waiting.old: Nest Ship at {colony} is waiting for colony population to reach {min_pop}.
notify.nest_waiting.new: Nest Ship at {colony} waits until population reaches {min_pop}.

notify.nest_drained.old: Colony drained 1 pop to launch a nest ship.
notify.nest_drained.new: A Nest Ship launched and took 1 pop with it.

ui.label.colonize.why: Match hardcoded UI and GDD spelling (American).

ui.fleet.doomstack_tip.old: You may rename it back. Brenda will not respect the rename.
ui.fleet.doomstack_tip.new: Eight or more ships in one fleet. You may rename it back. Brenda will not respect the rename.

refuse.not_owner.new: You do not own this colony.

refuse.tech_locked.new: Requires a technology you have not researched.

refuse.unsupported_climate.old: Planet climate does not support this.
refuse.unsupported_climate.new: Cannot be built on this climate.

refuse.invalid_jobs.new: Jobs must add up to the colony's population.

refuse.buy_filler.new: Trade Goods and Research Projects cannot be bought.

refuse.design_slot.old: At most one plate, mantle, or computer slot allowed.
refuse.design_slot.new: Only one plate, one mantle and one computer per design.

refuse.design_specials.new: Too many specials for this hull.

refuse.tech_unknown.new: Requires a technology you have not researched.

refuse.design_loot.old: Loot parts are only available to the looting empire.
refuse.design_loot.new: Only the empire that took this part can fit it.

refuse.design_limit.new: Active design limit reached. Mark an old design obsolete first.

refuse.design_in_use.old: Design is currently in production or in use.
refuse.design_in_use.new: This design is in production or flying. Mark it obsolete instead.

refuse.not_habitable.old: Planet is not habitable for this species.
refuse.not_habitable.new: Your species cannot live on this planet.

refuse.no_pod.old: Fleet does not contain a colonization or outpost pod.
refuse.no_pod.new: This fleet carries no Nest Pod or Perch Pod.

refuse.not_here.old: Fleet is not in orbit of the target planet's star system.
refuse.not_here.new: The fleet must be at the target planet's star.

battle.plan.swat.tip.old: Swat Priority: Determines whether Swat mounts intercept incoming missiles or fire at enemy ships.
battle.plan.swat.tip.new: Swat Mounts: shoot down incoming missiles first, or fire at ships like any other gun.

role.talon_line.tip.old: Beams. They want the middle of the strip.
role.talon_line.tip.new: Beam warship. Fights at Talon range, the middle of the strip.

role.beak_line.tip.old: Kinetics. They want the short end of the strip.
role.beak_line.tip.new: Kinetic warship. Fights at Beak range, point blank.

role.horizon_line.tip.old: Missiles. They want the far end of the strip.
role.horizon_line.tip.new: Missile warship. Fights at Horizon range, the far end of the strip.

role.horizon_boat.tip.old: A hull that tells the truth about what you think combat is.
role.horizon_boat.tip.new: All missiles, no beams. A hull that tells the truth about what you think combat is.

role.swat_escort.tip.old: It shoots the mail. Bring it when the autopsy said Horizon.
role.swat_escort.tip.new: Swat Mounts that shoot down incoming missiles. Bring one when the autopsy said Horizon.

role.boot_ship.tip.new: Troop transport for invasions. Marines, in a can.

role.nest_ship.tip.new: Colony ship. Founds a colony and is spent on landing.

role.stake_ship.tip.old: A claim with fuel range attached.
role.stake_ship.tip.new: Outpost ship. Plants an outpost that extends your fuel range.

role.glance.tip.old: Eyes. Auto-explore is the point of it.
role.glance.tip.new: Scout. Cheap, unarmed, built for Auto-Explore.

part.wick_talon.tip.old: A small light with opinions. It starts fights and finishes none.
part.wick_talon.tip.new: Talon, 3-8 damage. The starter beam: it starts fights and finishes none.

part.sun_quill.tip.old: Fusion, written in a straight line.
part.sun_quill.tip.new: Talon, 5-12 damage. Fusion, in a straight line.

part.banded_glare.tip.old: It arrives in stripes. The stripes are not decorative.
part.banded_glare.tip.new: Talon, 8-18 damage. It arrives in stripes, and the stripes are not decorative.

part.last_glare.tip.old: The evening-ender. The Guardian still flies the original.
part.last_glare.tip.new: Talon, 14-32 damage. The best beam there is. The Guardian of Orn flies six.

part.peck_driver.tip.old: A small hard opinion. Best delivered personally.
part.peck_driver.tip.new: Beak, 5-9 damage, shields count half. Best delivered point blank.

part.clatter_bill.tip.new: Beak, 9-15 damage. Many small opinions, quickly.

part.gizzard_bore.tip.old: It grinds. Range is a courtesy it declines.
part.gizzard_bore.tip.new: Beak, 14-24 damage. It grinds. Range is a courtesy it declines.

part.anvil_beak.tip.old: The shot has read about gravity and taken it personally.
part.anvil_beak.tip.new: Beak, 20-34 damage. The heaviest gun in the game, if you can get close.

part.hatch_dart.tip.old: The first thing a navy learns to throw away.
part.hatch_dart.tip.new: Horizon, 5 damage, 3 salvos. The first missile a navy learns to throw away.

part.ink_dart.tip.new: Horizon, 9 damage, +10 accuracy, 3 salvos. The invoice, in a hurry.

part.cited_dart.tip.new: Horizon, 13 damage, +15 accuracy, 3 salvos. More citations, same destination.

part.indoor_torpedo.tip.old: Unlimited, every other round. Indoor voices were requested.
part.indoor_torpedo.tip.new: Horizon, 30 damage. Unlimited ammo, fires every other round. Indoor voices were requested.

part.primary_mount.tip.old: Twice the space, half again the anger, and the falloff finally behaves.
part.primary_mount.tip.new: Talon mount: double space, x1.5 damage, half the range falloff.

part.swat_mount.tip.old: It shoots the mail before the mail arrives.
part.swat_mount.tip.new: Talon mount: half size, half damage, +20 accuracy. Shoots down incoming missiles.

part.walk_drive.tip.old: Map 2, combat 1. You are walking, and everyone can see it.
part.walk_drive.tip.new: Map speed 2, combat speed 1. You are walking, and everyone can see it.

part.current_drive.tip.old: Map 3, combat 2. A polite speed, until someone leans on it.
part.current_drive.tip.new: Map speed 3, combat speed 2. A polite speed.

part.fold_drive.tip.old: Map 4, combat 2. Space, pinched, and the pinching is licensed.
part.fold_drive.tip.new: Map speed 4, combat speed 2. Space, pinched. The pinching is licensed.

part.migration_drive.tip.old: Map 6, combat 3. The victory drive is this one.
part.migration_drive.tip.new: Map speed 6, combat speed 3. The drive you leave the galaxy with.
part.migration_drive.tip.why: Label the numbers; clearer victory nod.

part.pinfeather_plate.tip.old: Hull at face value. A suggestion of armour.
part.pinfeather_plate.tip.new: No hull bonus. Armor, as a suggestion.

part.joined_plate.tip.old: Seams, done properly. Half again the hull.

part.keel_plate.tip.old: Twice the hull. The bone, worn on the outside.
part.keel_plate.tip.new: Hull x2. The bone, worn on the outside.

part.marrow_plate.tip.old: Dense enough that the drive notices.
part.marrow_plate.tip.new: Hull x2.75. Dense enough that the drive notices.

part.unsinkable_plate.tip.old: Three and a half times the hull. The vote has been noted.
part.unsinkable_plate.tip.new: Hull x3.5. The argument is settled.

part.dust_cover.tip.old: Class 2. Stops a rude remark, and very little of a missile.
part.dust_cover.tip.new: Shield 2: every hit does 2 less. Stops a rude remark and very little of a missile.
part.dust_cover.tip.why: Explain what a shield class does.

part.half_mantle.tip.old: Class 4. Wings at half. The shot pays a toll.

part.full_mantle.tip.old: Class 6. Most of the evening stays outside.
part.full_mantle.tip.new: Shield 6: every hit does 6 less. Most of the evening stays outside.

part.closed_season.tip.old: Class 9. Nothing in season may be shot.
part.closed_season.tip.new: Shield 9: every hit does 9 less. Nothing is in season.

part.pecking_logs.tip.new: Computer, +10 accuracy. It remembers who bit whom.

part.predictive_peck.tip.old: The shot leads the duck. The ducks have written.
part.predictive_peck.tip.new: Computer, +20 accuracy. The shot leads the duck. The ducks have complained.

part.grudge_ledger.tip.new: Computer, +30 accuracy. Accuracy with a memory.

part.preened_cognition.tip.old: The ship thinks. The union has questions.
part.preened_cognition.tip.new: Computer, +40 accuracy. The ship thinks. The union has questions.

part.nest_pod.tip.old: A colony, packed. Spent on landing.
part.nest_pod.tip.new: Founds a colony. Takes 1 pop from the colony that builds it; spent on landing.
part.nest_pod.tip.why: The pop drain is the decision.

part.perch_pod.tip.old: A claim, and the fuel range that comes with it.
part.perch_pod.tip.new: Plants an outpost, which extends your fuel range.

part.boot_pod.tip.old: Four marines. The can is not the argument.
part.boot_pod.tip.why: 'The can is not the argument' is noise.

part.rude_sun.tip.old: Bombardment, doubled. Stacks to triple if you are that kind of guest.
part.rude_sun.tip.new: Bomb. Twice a Bomb Bay's bombardment, for that kind of guest.
part.rude_sun.tip.why: Old numbers did not match GDD.

part.very_polite_warhead.tip.old: It observes the forms. Then it is a sun.
part.very_polite_warhead.tip.new: Planet-killer bomb: eight Bomb Bays' worth, ignores planet shields. It observes the forms. Then it is a sun.

part.roost_bracing.tip.old: Half again the hull, and no apology.

part.miss_field_1.tip.old: Incoming Horizon is less convinced, by 20.
part.miss_field_1.tip.new: Incoming missiles get -20 accuracy against this ship.

part.miss_field_2.tip.old: Incoming Horizon is less convinced, by 40.
part.miss_field_2.tip.new: Incoming missiles get -40 accuracy against this ship.

part.loadout_glance.tip.old: +10 accuracy, and you may read their design.

part.crop_tanks.tip.old: +3 fuel range. The frontier moves out by three.

part.self_sealing_nest.tip.old: The ship apologises to itself and continues.
part.self_sealing_nest.tip.new: Repairs 10% of max hull every round. The ship apologizes to itself and continues.

part.gone_to_molt.tip.old: Untargetable in rounds 1 and 2. You may still fire. This is legal.
part.gone_to_molt.tip.new: Cannot be targeted in rounds 1 and 2. Still fires. This is legal.

part.not_this_feather.tip.old: A quarter of the shots were confident about a bird that had stepped aside.
part.not_this_feather.tip.new: 25% of hits on this ship miss outright.
part.not_this_feather.tip.why: Worst offender: a riddle for a stat.

part.orn_plating.tip.old: Salvaged from a guardian who had a prior appointment with your century.
part.orn_plating.tip.new: Hull +40%, shield +2. Salvaged from the Guardian of Orn; only its killer may fit it.
part.orn_plating.tip.why: Effect first; the Guardian nod kept.

ui.fleet.swat_options.tip.new:
Missiles: shoot down incoming missiles before they hit.
Ships: fire at enemy ships only.

ui.fleet.in_transit.new: In transit to Star %d, %d turns out
ui.fleet.in_transit.for: src/ui/screens/FleetPanel.gd:210 (code should pass the star name, not the id)

ui.fleet.colonize.tip.new: Found a colony on a planet here

ui.fleet.colonize.none_tip.new: No planet here your species can colonize

ui.fleet.outpost.tip.new: Plant an outpost here to extend fuel range

ui.fleet.outpost.none_tip.new: No planet here for an outpost

ui.topbar.credits.tip.new:
Income +%d (taxes %d, buildings %d, food sold %d)
Expenses -%d (ship upkeep %d, colony admin %d)
Net %+d

ui.topbar.food.tip.new:
Produced %d
Eaten %d
Surplus %+d (sells at 2 food per credit)

autopsy.victor.for: P04_autopsy row 1 (shows 'Empire 0'; pass the empire name)

autopsy.flavor.1.new: {victor} held the field. {loser} held a grudge.

autopsy.flavor.2.new: Read the band. It decided this before anyone pressed Skip.

autopsy.flavor.3.new: {ship} did the work. The rest of the fleet was present.

autopsy.flavor.4.new: Retreat works. It always leaves someone last.

autopsy.flavor.5.new: {loser} brought the wrong range to the right fight.

autopsy.flavor.6.new: The tier list was consulted. {victor} was on it.

autopsy.flavor.7.new: The autopsy writes itself. It paused less than you did.

autopsy.flavor.8.new: Shields subtract. Swats swat. Beaks need to be close. Someone forgot one of those.

autopsy.flavor.9.new: {victor} will call this decisive. The Perch Review will use the small word.

autopsy.flavor.10.new: Luck was involved. So was the design screen. Check the second one.

autopsy.flavor.11.new: Orbit belongs to {victor}. The paperwork belongs to {loser}.

autopsy.flavor.12.new: Nobody is OP at a range they never reached.

battle.orders.projection.new: Closing: Talon range by round {talon_round}, Beak by round {beak_round}
battle.orders.projection.for: P04_battle_orders row 3 ('Projection: Talon by round 2, Beak by 5')

battle.orders.automated.body.new: These fights use each fleet's standing battle plan:

ui.battle.range_strip.tip.new: Beak 0-3, Talon 3-7, Horizon 7+. Each side moves toward its posture's range; same speed still closes one step a round, faster closes sooner.

renames.why: A planet row reading 'Sour' does not tell a player the world is hostile; also affects the tech line 'Dome Perches (colonise Bare/Cinder/Sour)' wording if it is ever shown. Star name 'Sourwell' can stay.
Same reason; 'Crackle Shutters' tech name can stay as a proper noun.
Star class labels are a lookup column, not a joke slot.

Spelling split: hardcoded Fleet panel says Colonize, refuse.owned says colonized, GDD says colonise. Pick American everywhere (armor, apologizes); 'rumour' and 'armour' removed in the revisions above.

missing: Autopsy card (P04_autopsy): no flavour line, and 'Victor: Empire 0' prints an id. Added autopsy.title/victor/deciding_band/standout/receipt/receipt.none and autopsy.flavor.1-12 ({victor} {loser} {ship} placeholders must be supplied by code).

Battle Orders card (P04_battle_orders): every label and option is hardcoded. Added battle.orders.* with shorter labels ('Swat Mounts:' for 'Swat Escort Mode:', 'If odds under 50%' for 'Half (< 50% Odds)', 'Accept Orders' for 'Accept This Card'). The 'Projection' line is renamed 'Closing' so a player knows it is about range, not victory.
Range strip (P04): no tooltip explaining the bands or the closing rule. Added ui.battle.range_strip.tip.
Fleet panel (P03_fleet_panel): location/speed/ETA/toggle strings hardcoded. Added ui.fleet.* keys. The ETA line should name the star, not 'Star %d'.
Top bar tooltips (P02_galaxy_topbar): credits and food breakdowns hardcoded. Added ui.topbar.credits.tip and ui.topbar.food.tip (food tip now says the 2:1 sale rate).

System panel (P01_system_panel): 'Homeworld: %s' hardcoded; added ui.system.homeworld. Climate line prints 'normal gravity' in lowercase next to Title Case words; a ui.gravity.{low,normal,high} set is wanted.

Designer (P03_designer): 'Mark Obsolete' hardcoded; added ui.label.mark_obsolete. 'Expected Dmg/Rnd (d=3, vs shld 0/2/4/6/9)' needs a plain label such as 'Damage per round at range 3 vs shield 0/2/4/6/9' (string lives in the scene; no key given here).

New game (P01_new_game): the 'Tiny (Sub)' preset shows a placeholder subtitle; menu.preset.tiny.sub does not exist. Suggested value: 'Twelve stars. A lunch break.' (star count to be confirmed against the preset).

Not touched on purpose: race names/pitches/leaders, star names, hull names, trait names, splash lines, credits, Evening Standard subtitle, DOOMSTACK label, filler tips, Trade Goods/Research Project, the ui.label.* one-worders, 'Lock Governor' (meaning unclear from the capture but no better 2-word label without reading the code), the seed default 'FOWL' (a value, not copy) and PerfOverlay (debug).
